submission.natural_language_explanation: The positive pole is a retrospective word detector for the vocabulary of specialized professional, technical and institutional domains: it fires on field, sector and discipline nouns (finance, education, healthcare, engineering, chemistry, linguistics, history, law, medicine, retail, marketing, agriculture, industry, sports) and on the relational adjectives and technical nouns of those domains (medical, clinical, financial, economic, environmental, cognitive, behavioral, molecular, immune, actuarial, photovoltaic, fiscal, systolic; health, market, credit, tax, insurance, employment, cancer, diabetes, security), peaking on that word at roughly 0.2-3.8 against the scan's 0.49 maximum and most strongly inside multi-word technical or institutional terms ('Financial Surveillance Section', 'cognitive neuroscience', 'mental health problems'). It is not a next-token predictor (Jacobian-lens kurtosis 3.1, zero lens overlap, and ablating the pole moves the next-token distribution by KL 6e-5 with no concentrated target), and it stays at exactly zero on everyday narrative vocabulary (table, cup, kitchen, cat, bread, kettle, lantern, bicycle, umbrella), generic abstract nouns (idea, question, reason, time, world), generic adjectives (important, various) and person/role nouns (professor, consultant, surgeon, cardiologist, lawyer, engineer), even when those name the same field; strength is context-modulated, so a domain word in an ordinary frame can fall toward the 0.12 active threshold while the same word in a technical term reaches several times the scan maximum.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
On Saturday morning I woke before the alarm, made a pot of tea, and watched the rain slide down the kitchen window. The cat had already claimed the warm spot on the chair, so I left him there and cut a slice of bread. There was nothing urgent to do. I swept the floor, watered the plants on the sill, and put the kettle on again for a second cup.

By nine the rain had stopped. I walked to the corner shop for milk and eggs, past the library and the old bicycle leaning against the fence. The street was quiet. A man in a green coat was washing his car with a bucket and a long-handled brush, and two children were drawing on the pavement with chalk. The air smelled of wet leaves and the gutters were still running. I bought what I needed, exchanged a few words with the shopkeeper about the weather, and walked home slowly, stopping once to watch a dog chase a pigeon across the square.

The afternoon passed in small tasks. I oiled the hinge on the cupboard door, sorted a drawer of old photographs, and found the missing umbrella behind the boots in the hall. The drawer was full of things I had not looked at in years: old keys, a broken watch, a ticket stub from a concert I could no longer remember. I meant to read, but I fell asleep on the sofa with the book open on my chest, and woke to the sound of the neighbour's dog barking at a delivery van. For a while I simply sat by the window and watched the light change on the bricks of the house across the street.

In the evening I made soup and called my sister. We talked about her garden, the fence her neighbour had built, and a film she had seen at the weekend. She told me about a cousin I barely remembered, and about a wedding planned for the spring, and I listened while the soup cooled in the bowl. She sounded tired but cheerful, and she asked whether I had been sleeping. After we hung up I washed the dishes, folded the laundry, and sat by the window until the light went. It had been a slow, ordinary day, the kind I used to find dull and now rather liked.

On Monday the clinical trial would begin, and the oncology team had asked me to arrive by seven for the first infusion.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A long mundane narrative built almost entirely from the hypothesis's explicit zero vocabulary, with a single 'clinical trial' and 'oncology' sentence buried at the end, testing that the domain term still fires deep in context while the everyday words stay cold.
